label.trigger: jsonpickle.encode(...) is called with any non-None handler_context while the value being encoded is handled by a registered handler whose flatten method keeps the classic two-argument form, for example a datetime, a UUID, a compiled regex or a user handler written against BaseHandler.
label.expected_impact: The pickler always adds handler_context as a keyword when calling flatten, so every such handler fails with TypeError about an unexpected keyword. Encoding with a context then breaks for built-in types and for older third-party handlers, although the hook was meant to be opt-in and decoding of the same data keeps working.

context_locations.note: The registry module provides a signature probe for exactly this decision; the encoding path no longer consults it.

anchors.start: def flatten(self, obj: Any, data: dict[str, Any]) -> HandlerReturn:

context_locations.note: The documented handler interface takes only obj and data, and the built-in handlers such as DatetimeHandler in this module implement that form, so the context keyword is an optional extension.
The decoding twin still passes the context only to restore methods that declare it, which shows the intended contract and makes the encoder asymmetric.

known_counterevidence.note: Without a handler_context argument (the default None) nothing is added and every handler works, so the ordinary encode path and most of the test suite pass.
The call site that looks up and instantiates the handler is correct; the problem is only in how the helper builds the keyword arguments.

label.fix_summary: Ask the registry's signature probe about the flatten method first and add the context keyword only when that method declares it, mirroring the restore side, so two-argument handlers keep working when a context is supplied.

check.summary: Existing project module tests/handler_test.py: its case for a handler without the context parameter encodes with a context and must still round-trip; the module's other handler tests act as controls.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with system Python 3.14.4 and pytest 9.0.2: on before tests/handler_test.py fails only in test_custom_handler_without_context (TypeError: unexpected keyword argument handler_context) and the other 7 tests pass; on after all 8 pass. PYTHONPATH points at the work copy. The full project suite has two failures unrelated to the seed in this environment (test_load_backend and test_decimal_passthrough_handler fail on the unmodified pin too), so the check runs only the handler module. A manual run also showed that with the patch, encoding a datetime, UUID or compiled regex with a handler_context raises the same TypeError, while the pin round-trips them.
